title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: शि॒वेन॒ वच॑सा त्वा॒ गिरि॒शाच्छा॑ वदामसि । यथा॑ न॒-स्सर्व॒मिज्जग॑दय॒क्ष्मग्ं सु॒मना॒ अस॑त् ॥
pada: शि॒वेन॑ । वच॑सा । त्वा॒ । गिरि॑श । अच्छ॑ । व॒दा॒म॒सि॒  ॥ यथा᳚ । नः॒ । सर्व᳚म । इत । जग॑त । अ॒य॒क्ष्मम । सु॒मना॒ इति॑ सु = मना᳚: । अस॑त ॥

sayana.text: O Girisha, you who reside (shete) on the mountain (giri) Kailasa—we pray to you (tvaam) with auspicious (shiva), welfare-causing words in the form of praise. So that (yatha) our entire moving world (nah sarvam-it jagat)—the word 'it' is for emphasis—all beings including humans and animals, may be free from disease (ayakshmam) and endowed with a good mind (sumana). Do thus. (5)

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: "One should meditate on the Enemy of the Cities (Purari), shining with a body prepared for battle, with a gentle smile that is like a thunderbolt to the straw-like three cities, desiring to burn the demons, holding the Mountain-Lord (Meru) as a bow in his hand, and mounted on a chariot consisting of the assembly of gods." (5)
bhatta_bhaskara.text:
Now the second (of this pair). 'Shivenavachasa'. O Girisha—he who resides (shete) on the mountain (giri) Kailasa. Or, he who has the mountain as his excellent residence. Or, he who is the Lord (Isha) of the mountain (Kailasa), or the cloud (giri), or of speech (giraam) in the form of the Veda and Pranava. With auspicious speech (shivena vachasa)—with words of the nature of a hymn of praise, which consists of the recitation of your qualities, or which is welfare-causing, or which is pleasing to you—we speak (vadamasi) toward you (tvaam) who are endowed with all lordly qualities. We praise you—this is the meaning. 'Vadamasi' is the Vedic form for 'vadamah'. In the text, the word 'achha' has a long 'a' due to Vedic rules. The indeclinable 'achha' means 'toward'. Some say it is in the sense of 'to attain'.
...

12  

...say the etymologists. Indeed, with non-auspicious speech, the God might become angry. As it is said: "Let us not provoke you, O Rudra, let us not (offend you) with our salutations, O Bull, nor with ill-timed cries or joined invocations." Therefore, we praise you with auspicious words. If it is asked why, he says: so that (yatha) our entire moving world (sarvam-it jagat)—all beings, progeny, cattle, etc. The word 'it' includes stationary things like trees as well. 'Ayakshmam'—free from disease. 'Sumana'—here the gender changes; it means endowed with a good mind (soumanasya). 'Asat'—may it be so. It is the fifth mood (Let). This is the kind of thing for which we praise you. Or, in response to the question 'how?', he says: we praise you in such a way that while you are being praised, this (welfare) comes to pass.

For these two (mantras 4 and 5), the Purashcharana is continuous chanting for twenty-one days. Then, having completed the Purashcharana, one should perform the prevention of untimely death (akaala-marana) with these. A king should have it performed by a perfected Brahmin; then untimely death does not occur in the kingdom. With these two, one should offer a lakh (100,000) of oblations of sesame, rice, cow-ghee, and barley, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, over twenty-one days. In that kingdom, there is no fear of untimely death. In nine days, disturbances vanish. In eighteen days, untimely death is pacified in the whole world.

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
With an auspicious speech we address You, O Girisha — so
        that thereby all our world — cattle, sons, and the rest — may be
        free from disease and joyful.

Thus, having offered salutation in "namaste rudra," having prayed in the
second, third, and fourth [mantras] for the attainment of the desired and
the removal of the undesired by addressing Girisha — now [the devotee]
prays for the averting of his own fears along with a hymn of praise:
"shivena vacasa" — the word giri signifies the Vedas in their form as
syllables/speech; the Shruti confirms this: "tam ha trin girirupa-
navijnataniva darshayamcakara" (He showed them, as it were, three forms
in the shape of giri), and then explains: "veda va ete" (these are indeed
the Vedas). He who rests in (shete tishthati) the Vedas in their form as
giri (sacred syllables) is Girisha — the one who is declared/described by
the Vedas. O Girisha, we address (vadamasi, we extol) You with pure
(accha, unstained) and auspicious speech (shivena vacasa).

What kind of praise? That is described: yatha — in the manner by which,
when such praise is offered, all (sarvam it, all of it) our world (jagat,
the world of moving things in the form of cattle, sons, etc.) may be
ayakshma (free from disease), sumana (endowed with cheerfulness, happy),
and asata (may be so) — in such a manner do we praise [You]. Here, the
address "girisha" indicates that praise of the one who is declared by all
the Vedas is entirely fitting.

Therein, one might suspect that the words of a sinner are tainted by
association with sin. To counter this, the [deity] is addressed again with
"accha" (O pure one). Nothing adverse results from the association of the
pure (nirvadya) with the impure, even in such contact; just as the purity
of Ganga-water is not diminished by contact with gutter-water — rather,
by proximity to the Ganga, the very gutter-water itself becomes purified
and eventually becomes indistinguishable from pure water. Similarly, words
spoken by me that are directed toward the supremely pure Lord become
as worthy of respect as Vedic words — such is the intent of the address.
Hence, just as gutter-water fallen into the flow of the Ganga acquires the
character of the Ganga, so too my words acquire supreme auspiciousness
(shiva-tva) from such glorious association — with this thought the phrase
"shivena vacasa" is uttered.

This fifth mantra is in fact two verses (the fourth and fifth) combined into
one mantra. The seer of this mantra is of the Gautama lineage; the meter
is Gayatri; the deity is Rudra. The dhyana-shloka is: "May one meditate
upon the god blazing in his three-city-destroying form — the half-smile of
laughter, his divine bow ready to break the pride of the demons, mounted
on a chariot made of earth." Through these two mantras, [protection from]
untimely death and similar benefits are obtained. Perfection (purashcarana-
siddhi) is attained through continuous recitation for twenty-one days.

Thus [ends] the fifth mantra.

ऽपि मम नाभानेदिच्छष्येव त्वां भजत: पुत्रपौत्रादिकं पाल-
येति संबोधनाभिप्राय: । इति चतुर्थ: ।।

              शिवेन वचसा त्वा  गिरिशाच्छा
              वदानसि। यथा न: सर्वेमिञ्जगद्‌यक्षमं-
              सुमना असत् ।।

तदेवं नमस्ते रुद्रेति नमस्कृत्य द्वितीयंतृतीयचतुर्थैर्गिरिश-
प्राध्यनिष्टपरिहारौ प्रार्थेतौ; इदानीं स्तुतिपूर्वेकं तनुभयं
प्रार्थेयते— शिवेन वचसेति। गिरिशब्देन गिरिरूपा वेदाः
उच्यन्ते, तत्र श्रुति:— 'तं ह त्रीन् गिरिरूपानविज्ञातानिव
दर्शयांचकार' इति प्रस्तुय, 'वेदा वा एते' इति। तथा
च गिरिरूपेषु वेदेषु शेते तिष्ठतीति गिरिश: वेदप्रतिपाद्य:;
हे गिरिश, अच्छा निर्मलम्, त्वां शिवेन वचसा वदा-
मसि स्तुम इत्यर्थे: । कीदशी स्तुतिस्तत्राह— यथा येन
प्रकारेण कृतया स्तुत्या, न: अस्माकं संबन्ध, सर्वेमित्त्  सर्वे-
ऽपि, जगत् पशुपुत्रादिरूपं जङ्गमजातम्, अयक्ष्मम् अरोगम्,
सुमना: सौमनस्योपेतं सुखितं च, असत् स्यात्, तथा स्तुम
इति; अत्र गिरिशेत्यनेन निखिलवेद्वर्णेनीयस्य स्तोत्रं युक्त-
